have you tried quitting your project, removing your .godot folder, and try reopening the project again?
It was the fix of similiar problem from the beta.
I also experienced this in Android Editor and closing the affected file solved the issue.

Also reproduced it on windows. I can only reproduce it with `export_presets.cfg`.

My steps to reproduce it:-

- Open export_presets.cfg in editor.
- Export your project (I'm exporting it to Android).
- Minimise the editor and then maximise it again.
I actually fixed the problem just by closing all the scripts I had open and then reloading the project; after that, the problem went away for me. Hopefully that will help narrow it down somewhat.

> I can only reproduce it with export_presets.cfg.

That's somewhat expected. The presets are modified (re-saved) when exporting and it counts as external modification. It goes away when when you pick either option that deals with the file.

@KoBeWi - I've resolved it. The specifics of the case: I had a reference to a texture I had stored as a local shader parameter became invalid (purple and black checkers/missing texture). I've been using it pretty consistently for several weeks at this point, including having re-cloned my repository at some point. After deleting the .godot folder and re-opening the editor while hoping to solve this issue, the texture reference was missing even though it had not been moved or renamed. Godot 4.4 brings about the use of UIDs, and I did just upgrade my project, so that's why I'm curious about if /.godot has any relationship to the UID system.
There is UID cache in .godot, but it can be safely deleted and will be rebuilt automatically when missing.
Perhaps not when a project was recently upgraded with the UID generator tool.

I also just experienced this after upgrading to 4.4 stable from 4.3 stable on linux. In my case it happened with one specific gd script of no particular significance that I hadn't made changes to in weeks. It occurred reliably every time I ran the game from within the editor, and sometimes if the editor lost focus for a while. Not only were all of the timestamps reset on the affected file, but the inode number actually changed, as if the file was being replaced entirely with a copy. I did try closing and reopening the file, and also the whole editor, but the problem persisted. Removing .godot seems to have resolved it, but I haven't re-opened every single file and spent time using it after removing .godot. Will comment again if it recurs.

Don't know if it has any relevance, but I was toying with the new in-game editing tools, just selecting things not changing anything, and the editor crashed (leaving a frameless unresponsive game window). I do not recall if the problem started before this or not. The editor crashes on me fairly regularly anyway, but it's never done anything permanent like this before.

As an aside, realizing some random file is being entirely removed and replaced over and over for no known or intended reason deep in the bowels of months of work sure is disturbing. It might be good to offer via popup or checkbox to make a backup copy of the entire project before upgrading it. Even at the very least, a more stern warning like the UID thing.

I ran into this problem when I first upgraded my project from 4.3 to 4.4 and used the auto tool to help with the UIDs. Using the tool automatically opened all scripts from all scenes in the Editor, and I was getting this notification for 3 files on which I did no work. I closed all scripts in the Editor and the error stopped happening.

Managed to reproduce it from a copy made after upgrading my project but before removing .godot to fix it. Hope something in here helps narrow it down:

It is specifically triggered when saving any or all scenes, whether running the game or not. The editor doesn't notice the change until it loses and regains focus, but it's happening as soon as any scene is saved even if it has no relation to the affected script. So it naturally gets noticed most often when running the game from within the editor, which by default saves all scenes and switches focus.

Saving a script instead of a scene does not trigger it. Saving the affected script fixes it temporarily, until you close and reopen the editor. Closing either that script or all scripts doesn't fix it. It still happens if that script isn't open in the editor, you just don't see the change notification because it only watches open files. Having no scripts open and even a single unrelated scene open to be saved still triggers it.

So far, removing .godot is the only way I've permanently fixed it in my case, and it did hold up to some light use today with no unusual issues.

https://github.com/asymptoticdivergence/godot-file-modified-bug Open that, save any scene even without changes, alt-tab away and back, and it'll tell you health.gd was modified. Or at least it reliably reproduces it on my system.

In the process of reducing it I discovered that removing .godot/imported preserves the bug, but removing .godot/editor removes the problem. As such, you'll also see a lot of cfg files for deleted files in the editor dir, because apparently it keeps those around even when you delete the files through the editor.

I know my content isn't the point, but fair warning anyway: I am not to be held liable if the sight of such a mess drives anybody to gouge their eyes out of their sockets with a rusty spoon. That's why I don't mind sharing it, even though eventually I will refine it into an actual product: right now it's like that really broken car that you almost feel pity for any poor sap who tries to steal it
